q: The physics describing motion, called ____, was discussed in the previous chapter.
e: Kinematics is the branch of physics that describes motion without considering the forces that cause it.

q: This chapter is dealt with ____ which explains motion in relation to the physical factors that affect motion such as force, momentum, mass etc.
e: Dynamics is the branch of mechanics concerned with the motion of bodies under the action of forces.

q: A fundamental concept in dynamics is ____.
e: Force is a push or pull that can change the state of motion of an object.

q: Force is defined precisely by ____.
e: Newton's three laws provide the exact mathematical and conceptual definition of force.

q: Force can change the ____ of an object.
e: A net force is required to change an object's state of rest or uniform motion.

q: Newton's first law states that: When no ____ acts upon it, a particle at rest will remain at rest and a particle in motion at a constant velocity will continue to move with the same constant velocity.
e: An object will maintain its state of motion unless acted upon by a net external force.

q: In mathematical form, If ____ then $a=0$, $v=$ constant (or) zero.
e: Zero net external force results in zero acceleration, meaning velocity remains constant.

q: Newton's first law expresses the idea of ____.
e: Inertia is the tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion.

q: ____ is the natural property of a body which resists the change of its state of motion.
e: Inertia is directly related to the mass of the body.

q: In fact, the first law is often referred as the ____.
e: Newton's first law is synonymous with the law of inertia because it describes this fundamental property.

q: The net external force acting upon a particle is equal to the ____ of particle.
c: product of the mass and the acceleration
e: This is the core statement of Newton's second law of motion.

q: In mathematical form, ____
e: This equation mathematically represents Newton's second law, relating force, mass, and acceleration.

q: The direction of the acceleration is the same as that of the ____.
e: Acceleration is a vector quantity that always points in the same direction as the net external force.

q: It is equivalent to say that acceleration is ____ to force.
e: As the magnitude of the net force increases, the acceleration of the particle increases accordingly.

q: Therefore, second law is also called ____.
e: The second law directly relates the net force applied to an object to its resulting acceleration.

q: Newton's third law of motion states that: Whenever two particles interact, the force exerted by the second on the first is ____ to the force exerted by the first on the second.
c: equal in magnitude and opposite in direction
e: Forces always occur in pairs that are equal in size but opposite in direction.

q: In other words, for every action, there is an ____.
e: This is the common phrasing of Newton's third law of motion.

q: Action-reaction pair does not act on a single object but acts on ____.
e: Because action and reaction forces act on different objects, they do not cancel each other out.

q: In SI units, force that is acting on 1 kg mass to give it an acceleration of $1 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ is called ____.
e: The newton (N) is the standard SI unit of force.

q: Similarly, in CGS system a force that is acting on 1 g mass to give it an acceleration of $1 \text{ cm s}^{-2}$ is called ____.
e: The dyne is the unit of force in the centimeter-gram-second (CGS) system.

q: In FPS system the unit of force is ____.
e: The pound (lb) is the unit of force in the foot-pound-second (FPS) system.

q: The ____ is the unit of mass in British engineering system.
e: The slug is defined as the mass that accelerates at $1 \text{ ft s}^{-2}$ when a force of 1 pound is applied.
